title: Section 141 — Importation of girl or boy from foreign country

content.overview: BNS s. 141 — Importation of girl or boy from foreign country.
content.study:
Introduction and meaning
Importation of girl or boy from foreign country. BNS restatement of IPC 366B. Elements are substantially the same; cite the BNS number for offences on or after 1 July 2024. BNS restatement of IPC 366B. Cite the BNS number for facts on or after 1 July 2024.
In student language: BNS s. 141 is the rule on “Importation of girl or boy from foreign country”. The section provides that whoever imports into India from any country outside India any girl under the age of twenty-one years or any boy under the age of eighteen years with intent that girl or boy may be, or knowing it to be likely that girl or boy will be, forced or seduced to illicit intercourse with another person, shall be punishable with imprisonment which may extend to ten years and shall also be liable to fine. Do not stop at the heading. An examiner awards marks for the ingredients, the explanations and the illustrations, not for writing the title alone.

Why this is asked
Criminal law arguments turn on statutory ingredients. BNS s. 141 exists so that “Importation of girl or boy from foreign country” has a closed legal test in Chapter VI — Of Offences Affecting the Human Body. An authoritative analysis defines the concept, lists every ingredient, walks the statutory illustrations, states exceptions, and applies the test methodically to facts.
Chapter setting: Homicide, organised crime, terrorism, hurt, acid, restraint, assault, kidnapping and trafficking.

learningObjectives: Master the cross-border trafficking offence under BNS s. 141.
Analyze the age thresholds: girl under twenty-one years, or boy under eighteen years.
Understand the mens rea: intent or knowledge that the person will be forced or seduced to illicit intercourse.
Examine the statutory punishment: imprisonment up to ten years and fine.
Appreciate the gender expansion in BNS 2023 covering both girls and boys.
enhancement.definition: BNS s. 141 penalizes whoever imports into India from any country outside India any girl under the age of twenty-one years or any boy under the age of eighteen years with intent that such girl or boy may be, or knowing that it is likely that she or he will be, forced or seduced to illicit intercourse with another person, with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to ten years, and shall also be liable to fine.
enhancement.legalPrinciple: Prohibits transnational human trafficking by penalizing the cross-border importation of foreign minors and young persons for sexual exploitation.
statutoryFramework: Chapter VI — Of Offences Affecting the Human Body, BNS s. 141 (corresponding to IPC s. 366B with gender expansion).
Actus reus: Importing into India from any country outside India.
Protected categories: Any girl under the age of twenty-one years; OR any boy under the age of eighteen years (major BNS reform expanding to male minors).
Mens rea: Intent or knowledge that the victim will be forced or seduced to illicit intercourse with another person.
Punishment: Imprisonment of either description extending up to ten years, and fine.
essentialIngredients: The victim is a girl under twenty-one years of age, OR a boy under eighteen years of age.
The accused imported the victim into India from a foreign country.
The accused acted with intent or knowledge that the victim would be forced or seduced to illicit intercourse with another person.
enhancement.detailedExplanation: Section 141 targets international human trafficking. Under the colonial IPC (Section 366B), the law applied solely to the importation of girls under twenty-one years. BNS 2023 enacted a significant reform by explicitly expanding the statute to cover both girls under twenty-one years and boys under eighteen years, establishing gender-inclusive protection against transnational child trafficking. The actus reus is the cross-border importation into Indian territory from abroad. The required mens rea is the intention or knowledge that the imported minor/young person will be forced or seduced into illicit intercourse with a third party. The offence is complete upon the entry into India with the requisite intent; actual exploitation does not need to occur on Indian soil.
examples: Teaching example (Importing a 19-year-old girl): An accused arranges false travel visas to bring a nineteen-year-old foreign national woman into India under false promises of hospitality work, intending to hand her over to a commercial sex operation. The accused is guilty under s. 141.

Teaching example (Importing a 16-year-old boy): A trafficking syndicate transports a sixteen-year-old foreign boy into India to supply clients for sexual exploitation. Under modern BNS s. 141, this falls squarely within the expanded provision (up to ten years).
distinctions: Section 141 vs Section 97 (Chapter V): Section 97 covers child trafficking generally; Section 141 specifically deals with cross-border international importation into India.

Section 141 vs Section 143 (General Trafficking): Section 143 applies to domestic and transnational trafficking across all exploitation forms; Section 141 specifically penalizes the cross-border importation of young persons for sexual exploitation.
problemApplication: Issue: Whether a trafficker who brought a 17-year-old boy from a neighboring foreign country into India knowing he was to be exploited by a wealthy client is liable under s. 141.
Rule: Importing a boy under eighteen years from outside India with knowledge that he will be forced/seduced to illicit intercourse constitutes an offence under BNS s. 141.
Application: The victim was 17 years old, brought across international borders, with knowledge of intended sexual exploitation.
Conclusion: The accused is guilty under BNS s. 141 and faces up to ten years imprisonment.

Applies to girls under 21 years and boys under 18 years (expanded in BNS 2023).
